findings.description: F-002: «clock.tick(FPS) ... возвращает число миллисекунд, которые он прождал» (build_chapter_20.py:1301-1304) misstated the return value. tick() returns the time elapsed since the previous tick() call *including* any delay, not the delay itself; get_rawtime() is the wait-excluding method. Measured under pygame-ce 2.5.8: a frame doing 30 ms of work returns 30-31 ms with zero wait applied, while an idle frame returns 16 ms. Official docs (pyga.me/docs/ref/time.html): 'It will compute how many milliseconds have passed since the previous call.' This inverted the mechanism in exactly the slow-device case the section is about -- if tick() really returned only the wait, dt would be 0 on an overloaded device and delta-time movement would stall.
findings.resolution: Fixed in scripts/build_chapter_20.py: the sentence now reads «возвращает число миллисекунд, прошедших с предыдущего вызова clock.tick(), — то есть полное время кадра, включая ожидание, если оно вообще было». A new paragraph after the code block spells out the slow-device case (tick(60) returning 30 ms with zero wait when the frame's own work took 30 ms), explains that this is precisely why delta time rescues a weak machine, and points at clock.get_rawtime() for the wait-excluding value. Verified: «которые он прождал» returns 0 files in the rebuilt HTML while «прошедших с» and «get_rawtime» each return 1.

evidence.summary: Learning objective and scope: Diagnoses frame-rate-dependent movement in the 20.5 project and introduces delta time so speed is expressed in pixels per second rather than pixels per frame.

`x += dx` per frame makes real speed depend on the achieved frame rate. -- Confirmed -- notebook 20-16: `simulirovat_bez_dt(2, 30, 2) = 120.0` vs `simulirovat_bez_dt(2, 60, 2) = 240.0`, a 2x difference for identical code.
`x += skorost_x * dt` makes displacement independent of frame rate. -- Confirmed -- `simulirovat_dt(100, fps, 2)` yields exactly 200.0 for fps = 30, 60 and 120.

`clock.tick(FPS)` returns the number of milliseconds it *waited*. -- Was FALSE -- it returns milliseconds elapsed since the previous tick() call, delay included. Measured: a frame with 30 ms of work and no delay returns 30-31 ms. The wait-excluding value is Clock.get_rawtime(). Fixed under F-002.

Moving on both axes at full speed makes diagonal motion sqrt(2) ~ 1.41x faster; the fix is to normalise the direction vector. -- Confirmed -- `math.hypot(1,1) = 1.4142`; the project's own normalizovat() applies exactly this fix for the mouse push.
